notes.style: The stores are a single, exacting point of view on how a man should dress; the label follows it.
notes.craft: Sid Mashburn is a designer-retailer: its about page says it uses luxury brands' mills and makers but names none, and its stores' tailoring shops do alterations, not manufacturing. Product pages give a country on some items (Italy for a handmade shirt, Portugal for a trouser and a jacket) and describe mills generically ('an English mill'). A country of make and little else: 2, not 4.

craft_evidence.owned_d: About page: founded 2007 on Atlanta's West Side; eight shops with in-store tailors; says it uses 'the same mills, tanneries, and makers as capital-L-Luxury brands' without naming any. Services page: each store has an 'open-kitchen-style tailoring shop' (alterations, not garment making). No owned factory or workshop that makes the range.
craft_evidence.countries: Italy 1/6 (Otto handmade sport shirt), Portugal 2/6 (side-tab sport trouser, Ghost Rider jacket), not stated 3/6 (Virgil No. 3 tweed jacket, spread-collar dress shirt, fine-gauge Escorial half-zip). Sample of 6 PDPs: tailoring, shirts, trousers, knitwear, outerwear. About page says suits are 'made in Italy'.
